description: Underwrite an insurance policy from submission through risk evaluation, pricing, and binding.

steps.description: Receive and log an insurance submission with applicant and broker details.

inputs.name: submission-packet
inputs.desc: The application, supplemental forms, and loss runs from the broker or applicant

inputs.name: line-of-business
inputs.desc: The insurance line (property, casualty, professional liability, etc.)

outputs.name: submission-summary
outputs.desc: Structured summary of the applicant, requested coverage, and key data points

outputs.name: missing-information-list
outputs.desc: Items needed from the broker before underwriting can proceed

process: Extract the applicant name, address, industry, revenue, and employee count from the application.
Identify the coverage requested, limits, and effective date.
List any missing documents or data fields and flag them for follow-up.
Log the submission in the tracking system with a received date and assigned underwriter.

steps.description: Gather and organize the risk information needed for underwriting evaluation.

inputs.name: submission-summary
inputs.desc: Structured summary of the applicant and coverage request

outputs.name: risk-profile
outputs.desc: Complete risk profile including loss history, exposures, and controls

outputs.name: third-party-reports
outputs.desc: External reports collected (credit, MVR, inspection, industry benchmarks)

process: Request and collect any missing items from the broker.
Pull loss history for the prior 5 years and calculate loss ratios.
Order third-party reports as required by the line of business.
Compile the risk profile with exposures, controls, and loss trends.

steps.description: Evaluate the risk against underwriting guidelines and appetite.

inputs.name: risk-profile
inputs.desc: Complete risk profile with loss history and exposures

outputs.name: risk-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of the risk with a recommended risk grade and any concerns

outputs.name: underwriting-decision
outputs.desc: Preliminary decision: quote, decline, or refer to senior underwriter

process: Compare the risk against the underwriting guidelines and appetite for the line of business.
Evaluate loss trends, industry hazards, and control adequacy.
Assign a risk grade based on the evaluation criteria.
Make a preliminary decision and document the rationale.

steps.description: Price the policy by calculating the premium, selecting deductibles, and applying credits or surcharges.

inputs.name: risk-profile
inputs.desc: Exposures and loss data for rating

outputs.name: pricing-worksheet
outputs.desc: Detailed premium calculation with rate, exposure base, and adjustments

outputs.name: quote-terms
outputs.desc: Proposed premium, deductible options, coverage terms, and conditions

process: Apply the base rate to the exposure measure (revenue, payroll, units, area).
Apply experience modifications, schedule credits, or surcharges.
Calculate the final premium for each deductible option.
Document any coverage restrictions or endorsement requirements.

steps.description: Issue the formal quote to the broker or applicant with all terms and conditions.

inputs.name: quote-terms
inputs.desc: Proposed premium, deductible, and coverage terms

outputs.name: formal-quote
outputs.desc: The quote document delivered to the broker or applicant

outputs.name: quote-expiration-date
outputs.desc: The date the quote expires if not accepted

process: Compile the quote letter with coverage summary, premium, deductible, and conditions.
Set the quote expiration date (typically 30 days).
Deliver the quote to the broker or applicant.
Log the quote in the tracking system.

steps.description: Bind the policy on acceptance and issue the binder or policy documents.

outputs.name: bound-policy
outputs.desc: The bound policy with effective date, policy number, and coverage confirmation

outputs.name: underwriting-record
outputs.desc: Complete underwriting file for the policy

process: Confirm acceptance from the broker or applicant.
Issue the binder with the effective date and policy number.
Generate the policy documents and deliver to the insured.
Close the underwriting file and archive the record.

description: Adjudicate an insurance claim from first notice through investigation, liability determination, and settlement.

steps.description: Receive and log the first notice of loss, verify coverage, and open the claim file.

inputs.name: loss-notice
inputs.desc: The first notice of loss from the insured, agent, or third party

inputs.name: policy-number
inputs.desc: The policy number associated with the claim

outputs.name: claim-file
outputs.desc: Opened claim file with claim number, loss details, and coverage verification

outputs.name: coverage-confirmation
outputs.desc: Confirmation that the policy was in force and the loss is within covered perils

process: Log the loss notice with date of loss, date reported, claimant, and loss description.
Verify the policy was in force on the date of loss and coverage applies.
Assign a claim number and open the claim file.
Set the initial reserve based on the reported loss estimate.

steps.description: Assign the claim to an adjuster based on the claim type, severity, and geographic location.

inputs.name: claim-file
inputs.desc: The opened claim file with loss details

outputs.name: adjuster-assignment
outputs.desc: The assigned adjuster with contact information and target response time

outputs.name: investigation-plan
outputs.desc: Initial plan for the claim investigation (interviews, inspections, documentation needed)

process: Classify the claim by type (property, liability, auto, workers comp) and severity.
Select the adjuster based on expertise, workload, and location.
Set the investigation plan with required activities and timeline.
Notify the insured and claimant of the adjuster assignment.

steps.description: Investigate the claim through interviews, documentation review, and inspection.

inputs.name: claim-file
inputs.desc: Claim file with loss details and coverage

outputs.name: investigation-findings
outputs.desc: Findings from the investigation including statements, photos, and expert reports

outputs.name: liability-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of liability, causation, and damages

process: Interview the insured, claimant, and witnesses.
Inspect the loss site or damaged property and document with photos.
Collect and review supporting documents (police reports, medical records, repair estimates).
Engage experts (engineers, appraisers, medical reviewers) as needed.

steps.description: Determine liability and set the reserve based on the investigation findings.

inputs.name: investigation-findings
inputs.desc: Evidence and findings from the investigation

outputs.name: liability-determination
outputs.desc: Final liability determination with rationale and applicable coverage

outputs.name: adjusted-reserve
outputs.desc: Updated reserve amount reflecting the investigation findings

process: Evaluate the evidence to determine fault, causation, and the extent of damages.
Apply policy terms (deductibles, limits, exclusions, conditions) to the determination.
Update the reserve to reflect the expected payout.
Document the liability determination and rationale in the claim file.

steps.description: Settle the claim by negotiating the payout, issuing payment, and closing the file.

inputs.name: liability-determination
inputs.desc: Final liability determination and applicable coverage

outputs.name: settlement-agreement
outputs.desc: The agreed settlement amount and terms, including any releases signed

outputs.name: claims-adjudication-record
outputs.desc: Complete adjudication record for the closed claim

process: Present the settlement offer to the claimant or their representative.
Negotiate the final settlement amount if the initial offer is disputed.
Issue the payment and obtain a signed release where applicable.
Close the claim file and archive the adjudication record.

description: Administer an insurance policy through its lifecycle: issuance, endorsements, renewals, cancellations, and archival.

steps.description: Issue a new insurance policy in the administration system.

inputs.name: bound-policy-details
inputs.desc: The bound policy details from underwriting (insured, coverage, premium, effective date)

inputs.name: policy-forms
inputs.desc: The policy form set and endorsements for this coverage

outputs.name: issued-policy
outputs.desc: The issued policy with policy number, declarations page, and full form set

outputs.name: billing-setup
outputs.desc: The billing plan and first invoice for the policy

process: Enter the policy data into the administration system.
Generate the declarations page and assemble the policy form set.
Set up the billing plan (direct bill, agency bill, installments).
Deliver the policy documents to the insured and agent.

steps.description: Process mid-term endorsements and policy changes.

inputs.name: issued-policy
inputs.desc: The current policy to be endorsed

inputs.name: change-request
inputs.desc: The requested change (add coverage, change limits, update insured info, add location)

outputs.name: endorsed-policy
outputs.desc: The updated policy reflecting the endorsement

outputs.name: premium-adjustment
outputs.desc: The premium change resulting from the endorsement (additional or return premium)

process: Validate the requested change against underwriting guidelines.
Calculate the pro-rata premium adjustment for the remaining policy term.
Issue the endorsement and update the policy in the system.
Deliver the endorsement documents and updated invoice.

steps.description: Generate and deliver renewal offers for expiring policies.

inputs.name: renewal-underwriting-notes
inputs.desc: Underwriting notes on loss experience and any changes for renewal

outputs.name: renewal-offer
outputs.desc: The renewal offer with proposed terms, premium, and any changes from the expiring policy

outputs.name: renewal-deadline
outputs.desc: The deadline for the insured to accept or decline the renewal

process: Review the expiring policy terms and loss history.
Apply any rate changes, coverage modifications, or underwriting conditions for renewal.
Generate the renewal offer with the new premium and terms.
Deliver the renewal offer to the insured and agent within the required notice period.

steps.description: Handle policy cancellations and reinstatement requests.

inputs.name: cancellation-request
inputs.desc: The cancellation request with reason (insured request, non-payment, underwriting) or reinstatement request

outputs.name: cancellation-notice
outputs.desc: The cancellation or reinstatement confirmation with effective date and any return premium

outputs.name: policy-status-update
outputs.desc: The updated policy status in the administration system

process: Validate the cancellation or reinstatement request against policy terms and regulatory requirements.
Calculate the return premium or reinstatement premium.
Issue the cancellation notice or reinstatement confirmation within required timelines.
Update the policy status and notify all parties.

steps.description: Archive policy documents and maintain the policy record for retention requirements.

outputs.name: archived-policy-record
outputs.desc: The complete archived policy record with all documents, endorsements, and correspondence

outputs.name: policy-administration-record
outputs.desc: Summary record of the full policy lifecycle for reporting

process: Compile all policy documents, endorsements, billing records, and correspondence.
Store the archive per the document retention policy.
Set the retention period based on the line of business and regulatory requirements.
Generate the policy lifecycle summary for reporting.

description: Conduct an actuarial analysis from scope definition through data collection, method selection, calculation, and peer review.

steps.description: Define the scope and objectives of the actuarial analysis.

inputs.name: analysis-request
inputs.desc: The request for actuarial analysis (pricing, reserving, capital modeling, or rate filing)

inputs.name: line-of-business
inputs.desc: The insurance line and segment to analyze

outputs.name: analysis-scope
outputs.desc: Defined scope including the purpose, lines of business, evaluation dates, and methods to consider

outputs.name: data-requirements
outputs.desc: List of data needed (loss triangles, exposure data, rate history, industry benchmarks)

process: Clarify the purpose: pricing, reserve estimation, capital adequacy, or regulatory filing.
Define the lines of business, accident years, and evaluation dates in scope.
Identify the actuarial methods to consider based on the analysis type.
List the specific data sets required and their sources.

steps.description: Collect, validate, and organize the actuarial data.

outputs.name: loss-triangles
outputs.desc: Organized loss development triangles (paid, incurred, reported counts) by accident year

outputs.name: exposure-and-rate-data
outputs.desc: Exposure data, premium data, and rate change history

process: Extract loss data from the claims system and organize into development triangles.
Collect premium and exposure data for the relevant periods.
Gather rate change history and industry benchmark data.
Validate the data for completeness and consistency.

steps.description: Select and apply the actuarial methods appropriate for the analysis.

outputs.name: method-results
outputs.desc: Results from each applied method (development, expected loss ratio, Bornhuetter-Ferguson, frequency-severity)

outputs.name: selected-estimate
outputs.desc: The selected point estimate with the rationale for the method weighting

process: Apply the chain ladder (loss development) method to the paid and incurred triangles.
Apply the expected loss ratio method using on-level premiums.
Apply the Bornhuetter-Ferguson method as a credibility blend.
Compare results across methods and select the final estimate with documented rationale.

steps.description: Peer review the actuarial analysis for accuracy, reasonableness, and compliance.

outputs.name: peer-review-findings
outputs.desc: Findings from the peer review (data checks, method validation, reasonableness tests)

outputs.name: actuarial-report
outputs.desc: Final actuarial report with the selected estimate, supporting analysis, and peer review sign-off

process: Verify the data sources and reconcile totals against the source systems.
Check the calculations for arithmetic accuracy.
Test the reasonableness of the selected estimate against benchmarks and prior analyses.
Document the review findings and sign off on the final report.

description: Design a new insurance product from market research through coverage definition, rating, regulatory filing, and system build.

steps.description: Research the market need and competitive landscape for a new insurance product.

inputs.name: product-concept
inputs.desc: The initial product idea and target market

inputs.name: market-data
inputs.desc: Industry data, competitor filings, and customer feedback supporting the product need

outputs.name: market-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of market demand, competitive positioning, and target customer profile

outputs.name: product-requirements
outputs.desc: High-level requirements for coverage, pricing targets, and distribution channel

process: Analyze the target market size and growth trends.
Review competitor products, pricing, and coverage gaps.
Gather input from agents and underwriters on customer needs.
Define the product requirements including target segment and distribution.

steps.description: Define the coverage terms, conditions, exclusions, and endorsements for the product.

outputs.name: coverage-specification
outputs.desc: Detailed coverage specification including insuring agreements, conditions, exclusions, and definitions

outputs.name: endorsement-schedule
outputs.desc: List of optional endorsements with their coverage modifications

process: Draft the insuring agreements defining what is covered.
Define the conditions, duties after loss, and claim reporting requirements.
Specify the exclusions and any buy-back endorsement options.
Review the specification against regulatory requirements for the filing states.

steps.description: Develop the rating algorithm and rate tables for the product.

inputs.name: coverage-specification
inputs.desc: The coverage terms to be rated

outputs.name: rating-algorithm
outputs.desc: The rating algorithm with base rates, class codes, territory factors, and modification rules

outputs.name: rate-filing-support
outputs.desc: Actuarial support for the rate filing including loss cost analysis and expense loading

process: Analyze loss data to develop base rates by class and territory.
Build the rating algorithm with factors for exposure, risk characteristics, and modifiers.
Load expenses, profit margin, and contingency into the rates.
Validate the rates against target loss ratios and competitive benchmarks.

steps.description: Prepare and submit the regulatory filing for the new product.

outputs.name: filing-package
outputs.desc: Complete regulatory filing package (forms, rates, rules, actuarial memorandum)

outputs.name: filing-status
outputs.desc: Status of the filing in each state (submitted, approved, objected)

process: Compile the filing package with forms, rates, rules, and the actuarial memorandum.
Submit the filing through SERFF or the state-specific filing system.
Track the review status and respond to any regulatory objections.
Obtain approval and document the effective dates by state.

steps.description: Build the approved product in the policy administration and rating systems.

outputs.name: system-configuration
outputs.desc: The configured product in the administration and rating systems, tested and ready

outputs.name: product-design-document
outputs.desc: Complete product design document with coverage, rates, system configuration, and launch plan

process: Configure the policy forms and endorsements in the administration system.
Implement the rating algorithm in the rating engine.
Test the end-to-end quote, bind, and issue workflow with sample scenarios.
Document the product configuration and deliver the launch-ready product.

description: Place a reinsurance program from risk analysis through structure design, marketing, negotiation, and binding.

steps.description: Analyze the ceding company's risk profile and reinsurance needs.

inputs.name: portfolio-data
inputs.desc: The ceding company's portfolio data (premium, loss history, exposure by line and geography)

inputs.name: reinsurance-objectives
inputs.desc: The objectives for the reinsurance program (volatility reduction, capacity, catastrophe protection, capital relief)

outputs.name: risk-analysis
outputs.desc: Analysis of the portfolio's risk profile, peak exposures, and retention capacity

outputs.name: reinsurance-needs
outputs.desc: Identified reinsurance needs by type (proportional, excess, catastrophe)

process: Analyze the portfolio by line, geography, and loss experience.
Model the peak exposures and probable maximum loss scenarios.
Assess the company's retention capacity and risk tolerance.
Identify the types and amounts of reinsurance needed.

steps.description: Design the reinsurance program structure.

inputs.name: risk-analysis
inputs.desc: Portfolio risk analysis and peak exposures

outputs.name: program-structure
outputs.desc: Designed reinsurance program with layers, attachments, limits, and type (quota share, surplus, per-risk XOL, catastrophe XOL)

outputs.name: estimated-cost
outputs.desc: Estimated reinsurance cost by layer

process: Design the program layers with attachment points and limits.
Select the reinsurance type for each layer based on objectives.
Estimate the cost for each layer using market benchmarks.
Optimize the structure to balance cost and protection.

steps.description: Prepare the reinsurance submission package for marketing to reinsurers.

outputs.name: submission-package
outputs.desc: The reinsurance submission with company overview, portfolio data, loss history, and program structure

outputs.name: target-reinsurer-list
outputs.desc: Target reinsurers ranked by capacity, expertise, and relationship

process: Compile the submission with company financials, portfolio summary, and loss history.
Include the proposed program structure and pricing expectations.
Identify and rank target reinsurers by capacity and expertise.
Distribute the submission to the target reinsurers.

steps.description: Negotiate terms and pricing with reinsurers and bind the treaties.

outputs.name: bound-treaties
outputs.desc: Bound reinsurance treaties with final terms, pricing, and reinsurer participation

outputs.name: reinsurance-placement-record
outputs.desc: Complete placement record documenting the marketing process and final program

process: Collect and compare indications from the responding reinsurers.
Negotiate terms, pricing, and conditions with the lead reinsurer.
Finalize the panel with participating reinsurers and their shares.
Bind the treaties and document the placement record.

description: Conduct a loss control inspection from scheduling through site inspection, hazard identification, and reporting.

steps.description: Schedule the loss control inspection and prepare the inspector.

inputs.name: inspection-request
inputs.desc: The request from underwriting with the insured's information and coverage details

outputs.name: inspection-appointment
outputs.desc: Confirmed appointment with the insured including date, time, and inspector contact

outputs.name: inspection-checklist
outputs.desc: Customized checklist for the inspection based on the industry and coverage type

process: Review the underwriting request and prior inspection findings.
Customize the inspection checklist for the industry and hazard exposures.
Contact the insured to schedule the visit.
Prepare the inspector with background information and the checklist.

steps.description: Conduct the on-site inspection and document findings.

outputs.name: inspection-findings
outputs.desc: Documented findings from the site inspection with photos and notes

outputs.name: hazard-list
outputs.desc: Identified hazards with severity ratings and recommended corrective actions

process: Tour the premises following the inspection checklist.
Document conditions with photos and field notes.
Interview the site contact about operations, maintenance, and safety practices.
Identify hazards and rate their severity.

steps.description: Assign the risk grade based on the inspection findings and deliver the report.

outputs.name: risk-grade
outputs.desc: Assigned risk grade with supporting rationale

outputs.name: loss-control-report
outputs.desc: Complete loss control report with findings, recommendations, and risk grade

process: Score the inspection findings against the grading criteria.
Assign the risk grade (e.g., highly protected, good, average, below average).
Compile the report with findings, recommendations, and the risk grade.
Deliver the report to underwriting and the insured.

description: Pursue subrogation recovery from identifying recovery potential through demand, negotiation, and collection.

steps.description: Identify claims with subrogation recovery potential.

inputs.name: closed-claims-data
inputs.desc: Data on recently closed or settled claims

inputs.name: subrogation-criteria
inputs.desc: Criteria for identifying subrogation potential (third-party liability, product defect, negligence)

outputs.name: subrogation-candidates
outputs.desc: Claims identified as having subrogation recovery potential with the liable third party

outputs.name: recovery-estimates
outputs.desc: Estimated recovery amounts for each candidate

process: Screen closed claims against subrogation criteria.
Identify the liable third party for each candidate.
Estimate the potential recovery amount based on the paid claim and liability share.
Prioritize candidates by recovery amount and likelihood of success.

steps.description: Prepare and send the subrogation demand letter to the liable party.

outputs.name: demand-letters
outputs.desc: Sent demand letters with claimed amounts and supporting documentation

outputs.name: response-deadlines
outputs.desc: Deadlines for each demand response

process: Draft the demand letter with the claim facts, liability basis, and demanded amount.
Attach supporting documentation (paid amounts, investigation findings, evidence of liability).
Send the demand to the liable party or their insurer.
Set the response deadline and calendar the follow-up date.

steps.description: Negotiate the subrogation settlement and collect the recovery.

outputs.name: settled-recoveries
outputs.desc: Settled subrogation amounts with payment confirmation

outputs.name: subrogation-record
outputs.desc: Complete subrogation record for each pursued claim

process: Review responses from liable parties and counter-offers.
Negotiate the settlement amount considering litigation costs and probability.
Collect the agreed recovery and apply to the claim file.
Close the subrogation file and document the outcome.

description: Investigate suspected insurance fraud from red flag identification through evidence gathering, analysis, and referral.

steps.description: Screen claims for fraud red flags and prioritize for investigation.

inputs.name: claims-data
inputs.desc: Claims data including reported losses, claimant information, and claim history

inputs.name: red-flag-indicators
inputs.desc: List of fraud indicators (inconsistent statements, excessive claim amounts, financial stress, prior claims pattern)

outputs.name: flagged-claims
outputs.desc: Claims flagged for investigation with the specific red flags identified

outputs.name: investigation-priority
outputs.desc: Priority ranking based on the number and severity of red flags

process: Screen claims against the red flag indicator list.
Cross-reference claimant history for patterns (multiple claims, prior fraud referrals).
Score each flagged claim by the number and severity of indicators.
Rank the flagged claims by investigation priority.

steps.description: Gather evidence for the fraud investigation.

outputs.name: evidence-package
outputs.desc: Collected evidence including records, surveillance results, statements, and expert opinions

outputs.name: witness-statements
outputs.desc: Statements from witnesses, claimants, and involved parties

process: Obtain and review all claim documentation and correspondence.
Conduct recorded statements with the claimant and witnesses.
Order surveillance if warranted by the claim type and indicators.
Engage forensic experts (fire investigators, accident reconstructionists, medical reviewers) as needed.

steps.description: Analyze the evidence and refer confirmed fraud for action.

outputs.name: fraud-determination
outputs.desc: Determination of whether fraud occurred with supporting analysis

outputs.name: fraud-investigation-record
outputs.desc: Complete investigation record including referral to SIU or law enforcement if applicable

process: Analyze the evidence for indicators of material misrepresentation or fabrication.
Compare the claimant's statements against the physical evidence and records.
Make the fraud determination with documented rationale.
Refer confirmed fraud to the special investigations unit or law enforcement and deny the claim.

description: Plan and execute the insurance response to a catastrophe event from team activation through claims triage, emergency payments, and monitoring.

steps.description: Activate the catastrophe response team and establish the command structure.

inputs.name: event-notification
inputs.desc: Notification of the catastrophe event (storm, earthquake, wildfire, flood) with initial scope

inputs.name: cat-response-playbook
inputs.desc: The company's catastrophe response playbook and resource roster

outputs.name: activated-team
outputs.desc: The activated response team with roles, contact information, and reporting structure

outputs.name: initial-exposure-estimate
outputs.desc: Estimated policyholder exposure in the affected area (policy count, total insured value)

process: Declare the catastrophe event and assign the event code.
Activate the response team per the playbook (claims, underwriting, communications, IT).
Estimate the policyholder exposure by geocoding policies against the event footprint.
Establish the communication cadence and reporting structure.

steps.description: Deploy adjusters and set up temporary operations in the affected area.

inputs.name: initial-exposure-estimate
inputs.desc: Estimated policyholder exposure and geographic concentration

outputs.name: deployment-plan
outputs.desc: Adjuster deployment plan with assigned territories, lodging, and logistics

outputs.name: temporary-operations
outputs.desc: Temporary claims offices and contact centers established in the affected area

process: Determine the number of adjusters needed based on the exposure estimate.
Deploy field adjusters and assign territories within the affected area.
Set up temporary claims offices and mobile units.
Establish the local vendor network (contractors, restoration, emergency services).

steps.description: Triage incoming catastrophe claims by severity and fast-track emergency payments.

outputs.name: triaged-claims
outputs.desc: Claims categorized by severity (total loss, major, minor) with assigned adjusters

outputs.name: emergency-payments
outputs.desc: Emergency advance payments issued to policyholders with immediate needs

process: Receive and log incoming claims through all channels (phone, web, field, agent).
Triage each claim by severity: total loss, major damage, minor damage.
Issue emergency advance payments for policyholders with immediate living or business needs.
Assign claims to field adjusters based on territory and severity.

steps.description: Monitor the catastrophe response metrics and produce the event report.

outputs.name: response-metrics
outputs.desc: Dashboard of response metrics (claims received, inspected, closed, open, cycle time, customer satisfaction)

outputs.name: catastrophe-response-report
outputs.desc: Complete event response report with timeline, metrics, lessons learned, and reserve summary

process: Track response metrics daily: claims received, inspected, settled, and open.
Monitor adjuster productivity and customer wait times.
Update the aggregate reserve estimate as claim data matures.
Compile the final event report with timeline, total incurred, and lessons learned.
